audit.why: 54.74% over 654 games, marked HARD at 6/10 with an 8/10 carry threat. The shape is right: level 3 with a charged Grit bar is genuinely his, everything from level 4 onward is Camille's, and Sett does not reclaim the duel at items — his threat migrates to 5v5 rather than the side lane.

Spikes are stated accurately: Camille's level-2 Tactical Sweep, level-6 Hextech Ultimatum, and first-item Q-reset all-in; Sett's level-3 charged Haymaker and his first bruiser item. The claim that Sett is no hyperscaler and Camille keeps the 2+ item duel is consistent with his kit having no scaling steroid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three separate mechanics are described wrongly. (a) Haymaker is called a heal in four places — 'his W heal', 'his W-store can heal back'. (b) The Show Stopper is called a 'slow-then-suppress' and an 'R suppress'. (c) Facebreaker is written as an unconditional 'grab-stun' that 'roots you'.
audit.why: Riot's own text: Haymaker 'expends all stored Grit to gain a shield' — a shield, not a heal, which matters because Grievous Wounds does nothing to it and burst through it still lands. The Show Stopper 'carries an enemy champion through the air and slams them into the ground, dealing damage and slowing all enemies near where they land' — a displacement and a slow, no suppression. Facebreaker 'pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him, dealing damage and stunning them. If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned' — so in an isolated 1v1, the ability that is supposed to set up his whole combo only slows you. That is the single most decisive fact in this lane and it is absent. Facebreaker is 16s at rank 1 falling to 10s.
audit.corrected: Haymaker restated as a shield, The Show Stopper as a carry-and-slam with a landing slow, and Facebreaker's one-side-only slow written in with its 16s cooldown.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sett.json (Riot descriptions for W, E, R)

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Force every all-in while his E grab is on cooldown' has no number attached.
audit.why: Facebreaker is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s against Hookshot at 16/15/14/13/12s — they trade almost one for one early, so the window is real but short, and saying so makes the advice actionable instead of a slogan.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing tells you that standing alone on one side of Sett defuses his engage.
audit.why: Facebreaker's stun requires enemies on opposite sides of him. Against a lone Camille who has not dashed past him, it is a slow. The practical rule is to never let him get between you and your minions, which is exactly the mistake a Hookshot over the wave produces.

edits.before: His window: a fully-charged W is a stored true-damage Haymaker and his E grab-stun roots you, so a flat level-3 trade favors his grit.
edits.after: His window: a full Grit bar is a stored true-damage Haymaker, and Facebreaker only stuns if it catches you across him — alone it just slows.

edits.before: Even stage — his W heal and your Adaptive Defense shield cancel out, and the winner is whoever lands their setup first, your E or his grab.
edits.after: Even stage — his Haymaker shield and your Adaptive Defenses shield cancel out, and the winner is whoever lands setup first, your E or his grab.

edits.before: Hextech Ultimatum locks him in the arena with no walk-out, and your delayed-Q true damage plus W heal out-DPS his bruiser kit in the 1v1.
edits.after: The Hextech Ultimatum locks him in the arena, and your delayed Precision Protocol true damage plus Tactical Sweep sustain out-DPS him in the 1v1.

edits.before: Hextech Ultimatum locks him in the arena where he can't walk out; his only counter is his own R slow-then-suppress, and your delayed-Q true damage plus W heal win that isolated 1v1.
edits.after: The Hextech Ultimatum locks him in the arena; his only answer is The Show Stopper, which carries and slams you for a landing slow, not an exit — your delayed Q true damage wins that 1v1.

edits.before: Land E grab-stun to root you, then unload the stored W Haymaker true-damage for a burst trade
edits.after: Catch you across him with Facebreaker to stun, then dump the full Grit bar as Haymaker true damage

edits.before: Sett has no dash and no way to escape your E once you grapple, which is the spine of this lane — but level 3 is genuinely his. Don't take a flat auto trade once his W is fully charged: a max-stack W is a true-damage Haymaker, and his passive alternates fists for bonus damage, so trading straight up loses. Use Q at range to last-hit and chip his grit, respect the E grab line, and let his charged W expire before you commit. Your Adaptive Defense shield eats his first punch, so step in for the Q-reset only when his W store is empty.
edits.after: Sett has no dash and no way to escape your E once you grapple, which is the spine of this lane — but level 3 is genuinely his. Don't take a flat auto trade on a full Grit bar: Haymaker spends it all as true damage plus a shield, and Pit Grit alternates fists for bonus damage. Use Q at range to last-hit and chip his Grit, and keep your minions behind you — Facebreaker is a 16s pull that only stuns when it catches enemies on both sides of him, so alone you eat a slow. Your Adaptive Defenses shield eats his first punch.

edits.before: This is your lane. With a point in W and your Q cooldown dropping you out-trade him cleanly — E-in, W-slash for the max-HP damage and self-heal, then hold the ~1s for the delayed Q true-damage hit, and walk out on the Q move-speed before his grit converts to a counter-trade. At 6 your R is the kill button: lock him in the arena and he literally cannot leave, so his only answer is his own R suppress — and your W heal plus the Q true-damage proc beats that 1v1. Force every all-in while his E grab is on cooldown.
edits.after: This is your lane. With a point in W and your Q cooldown dropping you out-trade him cleanly — E in, Tactical Sweep's outer edge for max-HP damage and the self-heal, hold the ~1s for the delayed Precision Protocol true damage, and walk out on the move speed before his Grit converts. At 6 The Hextech Ultimatum is the kill button: he is locked in the arena, and The Show Stopper only carries and slams you for a slow. Force the all-in inside Facebreaker's 16s window.

edits.before: Sett wins by landing Haymaker, dragging Camille into a drawn-out fight while her E is down, and out-scaling or out-trading the side lane.
edits.after: Sett wins by getting between Camille and her wave so Facebreaker stuns, dumps a full Grit bar as Haymaker, and grinds the side lane down.

notes: Sett's kit file carries a derived 'grounding' flag on The Show Stopper, but Riot's description only mentions damage and a landing slow — no grounding. Since a grounding effect would deny Camille's Hookshot entirely and change the whole 1v1, I did not write it; worth verifying before anyone adds it. Packet suspectNames flagged 'Hextech Ultimatum' and 'Adaptive Defense' here: both were near-misses of the real names (The Hextech Ultimatum, Adaptive Defenses) and are corrected, but the substantive errors in this matchup were Haymaker being called a heal, The Show Stopper being called a suppress, and Facebreaker being written as an unconditional stun.
